IMPORTANT: This server provides best-practice skills that MUST be consulted before performing matching actions. Read the SKILL.md for the matching skill — it contains a Reference Files table that maps tasks to specific reference files. You MUST read the referenced files that match your current task before proceeding. Do NOT load all reference files upfront — only the ones the table directs you to.

How to access: Call ha_get_skill_guide() with no arguments: it returns SKILL.md. Then pass file='<path>' for each reference file the table points to. Use this tool even if your client can read the skill:// resources.

### Skill: home-assistant-best-practices (skill://home-assistant-best-practices/SKILL.md)
Home Assistant (HA) best practices. Load first, before answering or exploring, on any HA request.
TRIGGER THIS SKILL WHEN: - Creating or editing automations, scripts, scenes, dashboards, blueprints - Choosing template sensors, helpers, or Jinja macros - Restructuring triggers, conditions, or modes; button, remote, or event-entity automations - Renaming entities or migrating device_id to entity_id - Looking up card types or domain docs; writing AppDaemon apps - Deleting or restoring a backup, or upgrading Core or the OS
SYMPTOMS: - Jinja2 templates where native options exist - device_id used instead of entity_id - Entity IDs changed without checking consumers - Wrong automation mode chosen - Raw sensor or hard-coded value used where a helper belongs - Direct .storage edits or automation lookups there; generated YAML - User told to edit configuration.yaml for UI integrations - Hardcoded Blueprint entities or skipped selectors - Existing state changed with no recovery path - Jinja copy-pasted between templates

## Tool Discovery
Tools already in your tool list are callable directly — do not search for them. Once you hold a tool’s full schema, call it directly; repeat neither the keyword search nor the schema lookup for the same tool.

Most other tools are NOT listed directly — use ha_search_tools to find them.

WORKFLOW:
1. Call ha_search_tools(query="...") with ENGLISH keywords naming the operation (e.g. 'get entity state'). Translate other languages first; entity, area and device names keep their original spelling.
2. Results are compact: name, one-line description, a one-line params list and the proxy to use. Before calling, fetch the full description and input schema with ha_search_tools(tools=['<name>']). A tool already in your list comes back as a name-only stub (pinned: true) — use the schema you already have.
3. Execute the discovered tool — two options:
   a) DIRECT CALL (preferred): Call the tool directly by name. All discovered tools are callable without a proxy.
   b) VIA PROXY: For permission-gated execution, use the matching proxy:
      - ha_call_read_tool — safe, read-only operations
      - ha_call_write_tool — creates or modifies data
      - ha_call_delete_tool — removes data permanently

A few default tools are listed directly (ha_manage_backup, ha_get_overview, ha_report_issue, ha_search, ha_config_get_automation, ha_config_set_automation, ha_get_skill_guide) — these are the starting pins, and users can unpin the non-mandatory ones via the Tools tab in the settings UI, so the actual visible set may be a subset of this list. Everything else must be discovered via search.

DO NOT assume a capability is unavailable because you don't see a direct tool for it. ALWAYS search first.

## Filing ha-mcp issues
Before filing any GitHub issue about ha-mcp, feature requests included, run ha_report_issue and put the issue_body it returns in the issue unchanged. A bug report filed without it is closed automatically after 24 hours.
